items.title: Report: UK ‘not on track’ to meet 2030 biodiversity targets
items.summary: Ahead of the Biodiversity COP happening later this month, the Wildlife Trusts has emphasised that the UK is lagging on its nature commitments under the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF).

items.title: Methane abatement and carbon removal: Why climate strategies now run on two clocks
items.summary: Corporate net-zero plans are written in the language of carbon dioxide. But how companies keep score can obscure a timing difference that matters for how they build climate portfolios.

items.title: Google strikes 20-year nuclear deal worth $4.3bn
items.summary: The agreement with Constellation Energy is set to enable over $4bn of investment and bring 890 megawatts (MW) of new nuclear capacity online.

items.title: SPEAKERS ANNOUNCED: What SMEs need to know before investing in solar
items.summary: Two expert speakers have been confirmed for an upcoming edie webinar exploring how SMEs can overcome the financial and practical barriers to onsite solar and maximise the return on their investment.

items.title: ONE WEEK TO GO: Connecting existing sustainability reporting with UK SRS
items.summary: With just one week to go, sustainability and reporting professionals are invited to register for an upcoming edie webinar exploring how businesses can connect existing ESOS, SECR and TCFD-aligned processes with emerging UK Sustainability Reporting Standards (UK SRS).

items.title: Win a free VIP pass to edie 27: Take our sustainability snapshot survey
items.summary: Sustainability professionals have the chance to win six months of access to edie’s digital Membership offering as well as a VIP pass to edie 27 in April by completing a short survey.

items.title: From scrapping the Future Homes Standard to repealing the Climate Change Act: What the Conservatives’ economic plan means for the UK’s net-zero economy
items.summary: The Conservative Party’s shadow chancellor has announced plans to scrap a series of environmental and net-zero policies, including the Future Homes Standard and the Climate Change Act, as part of a wider programme of economic deregulation.

items.title: Business giants call for financial reforms to halt nature degradation
items.summary: More than 100 businesses and financial institutions have called on governments to kickstart a 12-month reform of subsidies and incentives that cause harm to nature and could impact long-term economic resilience, ahead of COP17 later this month.
